clauses.quote: The following filenames have defined meaning at any level of the hierarchy and MUST NOT be used for concept documents
`type` is the only always-required key; a concept carrying just `type` is fully conformant (§11).
consumers MUST tolerate unknown types gracefully, typically by treating them as generic concepts.
Consumers SHOULD preserve unknown keys when round-tripping and MUST NOT reject documents with unrecognized fields.
Consumers MUST treat a bare mapping as a one-element list
clauses.reason: okf-parser does not derive trust tiers; it preserves both shapes verbatim, which the verified-mapping-and-list case pins.

clauses.quote: A concept with no trust frontmatter is still consumable; consumers MUST NOT reject it (§11).
producers MUST use it for hand-authored or human-confirmed content.
clauses.reason: Producer obligation; a consumer cannot tell whether content was hand-authored.

clauses.quote: Consumers MUST tolerate broken links: a link whose target does not exist in the bundle is not malformed
Concepts MAY link to other concepts using standard markdown links. Two forms are supported:
Index files contain no frontmatter, with one exception: a bundle-root `index.md` MAY carry an `okf_version` key (§12).
Date headings MUST use ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` form.
The agent MAY only supply *values* for the declared `parameters`; it MUST NOT author or edit the computation.
clauses.reason: Runtime obligation on an executing agent, not on a bundle reader.

clauses.quote: Every non-reserved `.md` file in the tree contains a parseable YAML frontmatter block.
Every frontmatter block contains a non-empty `type` field.
Every reserved filename (`index.md`, `log.md`) follows the structure in §8 and §9 respectively when present.
Consumers that do not understand the declared version SHOULD attempt best-effort consumption rather than refusing the bundle.
A v0.1 bundle is consumable by a v0.2 consumer under the fallbacks noted here.
